name: Trade war & tariffs
value: Mexico doubling threat 12 Nov; not in force
summary: Trump's threat to double tariffs on Mexico is not in force; EU opens a third safeguard probe aimed at Chinese imports
state: Trump's 12 Nov threat to double tariffs on Mexican goods has not been enacted; Sheinbaum said after meeting Trump on 18 Nov that talks on steel, aluminium and car tariffs were very advanced and she hopes for a deal in December (Rio Times, 19 Nov). On 23 Nov the EU opened a safeguard investigation into resins and glass fibre, its third in under a month aimed mainly at Chinese imports (Aju Press). No broad new tariffs with retaliation under way were found, so Watch holds.
for_you: Importers and exporters trading with the US, Mexico, China and the EU face uncertainty over tariff rates and possible new safeguard duties. UK businesses can find official guidance on trade rules from the Department for Business and Trade.
rubric_hit: Watch: major new tariffs threatened between large economies (US doubling threat on Mexico, 12 Nov); not in force

sources.title: Rio Times — Sheinbaum expects US tariff-cut deal in December
Aju Press — EU widens trade shields against China

why: Tariffs raise prices, reroute supply chains and slow growth; escalation cycles hurt export-heavy economies like the UK's partners.
drivers: US tariff policy, retaliation, court rulings, trade deals, WTO disputes.

rubric.alert: Broad new tariffs in force with retaliation under way, or US average effective tariff rising sharply.
rubric.watch: New major tariffs announced or threatened between large economies.
rubric.normal: Tariff regime stable; no new major measures in the past two weeks.
